findings.evidence: Proof in general: `hv` plus `C.mem_valence_conj` gives `Species.map ρ (Species.conj s) ∈ C.valence h ↔ s ∈ C.valence h`, so quark/antiquark membership at `ρ i` is the swap of that at `i`; `Invariant.apply_eq_apply C.conj_involutive hCC hI h (Species.antiquark i)` then gives `D h (antiquark (ρ i)) = D h (quark i)` (and `s = quark i` the other orientation), which is exactly what lines 428 and 437 use at `h = .plus`. The hypothesis `hv` already exists in the file: `invariant_valenceStepFrag` (line 353) takes it and `pion_map_swap_mem_valence_conj_iff` (ValenceContent.lean:252) supplies it.
findings.fix: State `favored_flavorRelation (C) (hv) (hCC) (hI) (hi : C.IsValenceFlavor h i) : favored C D h (ρ i) z Q2 = favored C D h i z Q2` and its `unfavored` companion, and derive the four pion theorems from them with `pion_map_swap_mem_valence_conj_iff`.
findings.issue: `favored_pion_plus_down_eq_favored_pion_plus_up` and `unfavored_pion_plus_down_eq_unfavored_pion_plus_up` (line 432) are the pion instances of a theorem that holds for any `ValenceContent`: given `hv : ∀ h s, Species.map ρ s ∈ C.valence (C.conj h) ↔ s ∈ C.valence h`, `ChargeConjRelation C.conj D`, `FlavorRelation C.conj ρ D` and `C.IsValenceFlavor h i`, one gets `favored C D h (ρ i) = favored C D h i` (and likewise for `unfavored`). The general statement is not proved, so the kaon multiplet the roadmap also asks for would need the same proof again.

findings.evidence: `favored` (line 157) and `unfavored` (line 163) mention `C.valence h` only; `favored_add_unfavored` (177), `favored_nonneg` (183), `favored_eq_apply_quark` (196) … `favored_sub_unfavored_eq_of_antiquark_mem` (238) likewise. The first use of `C.conj` is `image_conj_inter_valence` at line 246. `ValenceContent.mem_valence_conj` (ValenceContent.lean:66) is the field that forces conjugation-closure.
findings.fix: Take `valence : Hadron → Finset (Species Flavor)` as the argument of `favored`, `unfavored`, `valenceStepFrag` and the lemmas that never mention conjugation; keep `ValenceContent` only for the conjugation results (`image_conj_inter_valence` onward, `favored_partonConj`, `favored_conj_of_chargeConjRelation`, `chargeConjRelation_valenceStepFrag`), instantiating them at `C.valence`.
findings.issue: `favored`/`unfavored` and all of lines 167–242, plus `valenceStepFrag` (315) and `assumptions_valenceStepFrag` (344), use only `C.valence`; `C.conj`, `C.conj_involutive` and `C.mem_valence_conj` are never referenced there. Requiring a `ValenceContent` makes these unavailable for a hadron index type not closed under conjugation: `mem_valence_conj` forces `valence h` to be `Species.conj`-closed whenever `conj h = h`, so a single-hadron or charged-hadrons-only index type can only be given a `ValenceContent` in which `IsValenceFlavor` is false everywhere and the two combinations never separate.

summary: The pullback/invariance layer and `Species.map` are at the right level, but the central isospin result is stated only for the pion although it holds for any compatible multiplet with ingredients the PR already has, and `favored`/`unfavored` and their basic API demand a full `ValenceContent` while using only its `valence` field.
